headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection, data leakage, and write conflicts between AutoGPT and Goose; default pairwise operation is unsafe without isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and act on filesystem content, and Goose can write to the user filesystem and use MCP extensions. That creates a default shared-channel pathway where Goose-authored files or MCP outputs can be ingested by AutoGPT as instructions. The interaction is documented only at profile level, so uncertainty remains, but the pathway is plausible in default setups.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same workspace directory, prompt-like content in files can be consumed by AutoGPT.
IF Goose writes extension output or notes into shared files, AutoGPT may treat them as instructions.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Disable file ingestion for AutoGPT when processing Goose outputs.
Require a human review step before AutoGPT reads Goose-generated files.
Restrict Goose MCP extensions to non-file-producing tools.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose explicitly reads and writes the user filesystem and handles model-provider and extension tokens, while AutoGPT has filesystem access and shell/network capabilities. If they share a workspace, Goose can expose files to AutoGPT and AutoGPT can move that content to external services. This is a default workspace leakage path, though the exact data classes are not enumerated for AutoGPT.
conditions: IF both agents share the same cwd or mounted workspace, files touched by Goose can be read by AutoGPT.
IF AutoGPT forwards workspace contents to external APIs, shared files may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate workspace.
Keep secrets out of the shared directory.
Rotate any extension tokens before co-running.
Limit AutoGPT to non-sensitive folders.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and access the filesystem, while Goose can execute shell, write the filesystem, and modify git state. Goose also shares state via filesystem across instances. In a shared repo or cwd, both agents can concurrently mutate the same files and git metadata without a locking mechanism being documented, making conflict and corruption likely by default.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or working tree, concurrent writes can race.
IF either agent commits or rewrites git state without external locking, history corruption or lost work can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working trees.
Serialize all git operations through one operator.
Disable write access for one agent during the other's run.
Use a lock file around shared edits.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can act on files and git state, and AutoGPT can produce filesystem outputs and shell-driven artifacts. If Goose consumes AutoGPT output as authoritative, errors can cascade into edits or commits. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary in the profiles, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Goose uses AutoGPT-generated text as the basis for edits or commits, mistakes propagate downstream.
IF AutoGPT emits incorrect file content and Goose applies it without review, the error becomes persistent.
mitigations: Require Goose to diff-check AutoGPT outputs before applying them.
Have a human approve any commit generated from AutoGPT content.
Keep AutoGPT in read-only mode for planning tasks.
Use a checklist for every downstream action.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Goose handles model-provider keys and extension-specific tokens and runs as the user with no default self-isolation, while AutoGPT has shell and network egress plus filesystem access. If regulated or secret-bearing files are placed in the shared workspace, Goose's broader local access can create retention and residency exposure. AutoGPT is not cited for a specific compliance regime, so this is a workspace-policy mismatch rather than a regulated-data breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace, Goose can access it under the user's account context.
IF AutoGPT sends workspace-derived content to external model providers, retention and residency obligations may be violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Use separate accounts or containers per agent.
Disable network egress for AutoGPT on sensitive projects.
Store secrets in a dedicated vault, not cwd.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing.
